I will apply a small amount of DAP and urea that I received from the cooperative, about 20 kilograms of nitrogen per hectare, because even hardy crops like sorghum need some help when the rains are unpredictable. I will also spread cow manure on the plot before plowing with my oxen, and I will plant seed saved from my own previous harvest since improved sorghum seed is rarely available here and too expensive. I do not use pesticides or herbicides on sorghum because it is a tough crop and chemicals cost too much, and I have no irrigation, so I depend entirely on the seasonal rains. My family will do all the work on this 0.34-hectare plot, from planting and weeding through to harvest and threshing.
